text: In the twenty-second chapter of Genesis a question is raised which is never answered. Abraham is commanded to take his son, his only son, whom he loves; of what he feels we are told nothing, for the narrator never once looks within him. He appears less as a character than as a silence, and upon that silence the whole chapter turns. He neither protests nor bargains; there is nothing in him here of the man who, on an earlier occasion, pleaded for Sodom.
